transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time at work lately. I do bookkeeping, and I just... I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

I end up staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I know I've already checked the numbers, I feel like I have to do it one more time. If I don't, I get this awful feeling that something bad is going to happen, and it'll be my fault. It's just gotten really out of control, and I didn't know what else to do.

When you feel the urge to check those spreadsheets again, do unwanted thoughts or images pop into your head that make you feel like you have to check — or is it more of a general worry or anxiety that drives you to do it?

It's definitely specific thoughts. Like, even after I check and I know the numbers match up, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake in the payroll or the taxes. I'll start thinking that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in trouble because of me. I try to push the thought away, but it just comes right back. It's like... I can't even trust my own eyes anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with classic obsessive-compulsive disorder characterized by intrusive obsessions (recurrent thoughts about hidden mistakes in calculations, fears of causing harm through payroll errors) that trigger compulsive checking behaviors (repeatedly reviewing spreadsheets and calculations). The obsessions are unwanted, cause significant distress, and the compulsions are performed to reduce anxiety. Functional impairment is evident through prolonged work hours and inability to stop the cycle despite recognizing the irrationality.
